articles.body: Alaska GOP Sen. Dan S. Sullivan can’t shake his same-name challenger. Retired teacher Dan J. Sullivan punched a ticket out of the state’s top-four, all-party primary early Wednesday morning. He could now play spoiler in a high-stakes Senate clash between the Republican senator and former Democratic Rep. Mary Peltola that could help swing control of the upper chamber. Republicans fought and failed to keep Dan J. Sullivan off the primary ballot , arguing he was a Democratic plant designed to boost Peltola. Both Dan J. Sullivan and Peltola’s campaign have denied any coordination. The senator’s allies have already taken steps to mitigate the second Sullivan’s potential vote siphoning, in some cases running ads using the senator’s middle initial to help differentiate between the same-named candidates. Supporters of the state’s ranked-choice voting system, which kicks in for the general election, argue the process helps curtail the spoiler effect. But the presence of other candidates could still skew the results of the battleground race. Outside groups flooded the primary with more than $2 million to boost myriad fringe candidates — and could do so again ahead of November. It’s not smooth sailing for Peltola, either, as she wages an uphill battle to flip a red seat in a state President Donald Trump won by 13 percentage points in 2024. She recently replaced her campaign manager in a staffing shakeup ahead of the primary, among other internal moves.
articles.headline: The other Dan Sullivan makes November ballot against Sen. Dan Sullivan

articles.body: President Donald Trump notched a major win on Tuesday night. Republicans in battlegrounds wonder if it was the best use of his time and money. Sen. Darline Graham defeated Rep. Ralph Norman in South Carolina’s snap Senate GOP runoff, handing Trump a revitalizing win after several of his endorsed candidates fell in recent primaries . It was a victory that Graham, a complete political unknown six weeks ago, could not have pulled off without Trump’s steadfast support , underscoring just how much his influence still matters among the Republican electorate in the deeply conservative state. But South Carolina’s Senate seat will not dictate the balance of power in Washington, and GOP strategists working on critical swing state campaigns are eager for Trump to finally direct his attention to them. “The message coming out of this is that obviously the president's support is still super powerful. The president's operation still has the ability to move the needle in a lot of these states,” said a Republican strategist working on several battleground races, including in Georgia, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about Trump’s involvement. “Hopefully, this is a sign of things to come that the president is willing to get involved and really start to move the needle in some other places that obviously matter a little bit more than South Carolina.” Trump’s persistent backing of Graham defined the race: He championed her appointment to her late brother Sen. Lindsey Graham’s seat, he coaxed her into the race with an early endorsement, stood by her as she stumbled on the debate stage , and flew down to Myrtle Beach for a rare political rally that few of his chosen candidates have enjoyed this cycle. MAGA Inc., Trump’s behemoth super PAC, even spent a slice of highly sought after cash from its $400 million stockpile in the closing days of the race. And yet, the president hasn’t taken a meaningful step into the states that will matter in a few short months — even as battleground Republicans have been clamoring for him to spend his MAGA Inc. money. “It's now or never. It's put up or shut up time, and it's really time to start to see if he's going to get serious,” the GOP strategist said. “You've got September and October to really move the needle here, and it just doesn't seem like there's any sense of urgency, or like we understand that we are down big in some of these states.” During her victory speech in Columbia, Graham acknowledged Trump’s heavy hand: “Our victory would not have been possible without you, and we are truly grateful,” Graham said of the president. “South Carolina is truly Trump country.” Norman’s take on the president’s participation was not as rosy: "The president got involved. He has that right. That's his prerogative,” Norman said in his concession speech Tuesday, prompting jeers from the crowd at his election night watch party. “Y'all,” he continued, “his policies are good. I never understood why he got in this race. It is what it is, and I'll accept it." Norman’s bewilderment reflected several national and South Carolina Republicans’ confusion as to why the president would expend energy for the safe Republican seat when his MAGA allies like Mike Collins in Georgia, scandal-plagued Ken Paxton in Texas and Michael Whatley in North Carolina are facing tough Senate battles against Democratic opponents. “There's the principle,” said a North Carolina-based GOP strategist who was granted anonymity to speak candidly about the battleground picture. “If you're not Trump and you have these people shoved down your throat, you're like, ‘Okay, are you gonna help?’” The White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Some Republicans are worried that though Trump helped power Graham’s win, the president’s overall unpopularity may be more of a curse than a boon in any highly competitive battleground state. A series of Trump-backed candidates lost gubernatorial and congressional primaries in recent weeks, including in Georgia and Iowa . Republicans overall are facing a tough election environment given the ongoing and unpopular war in Iran, backlash to the administration’s highly-visible deportation agenda and voters’ persistent cost of living concerns. “You have a president and maybe even a vice president that are just so underwater politically in the polls, that they might be a help by not intervening,” said Matthew Bartlett, a GOP strategist and former State Department official in the first Trump administration. Still, Trump swept the battlegrounds in 2024, and his ability to boost Graham despite her foreign policy debate gaffe and questions about her political inexperience serves as a reminder of his electoral prowess to campaign officials. The question remains when — or if — he’ll throw them a presidential life raft. “I wouldn't count on the money if I were in these states,” said the North Carolina-based Republican strategist. “He still could. I’m just saying, I wouldn’t count on it. We're not dealing with somebody that's, you know, super calculated in the way they plan.” For months, Republicans across the country have watched on as the president has continued to amass a remarkable pile of cash — and many have implored him to empty his pockets in their races . The president told reporters last week that he’ll spend “a lot of that money” to boost “Republican candidates that I think are good,” without being specific. However, what some saw as a distraction from the greater Republican cause this year, others read as the first few drops of Trump’s cash flood. “If they're going to spend 800 grand in South Carolina, they're going to spend in the midterms,” said Matt Mackowiak, a Republican strategist based in Texas who worked on Sen. John Cornyn’s failed reelection campaign and is now backing the GOP ticket. “It signals they're going to make a substantial investment in the midterms because you don't make an 800-grand investment in South Carolina and say, ‘Yeah, we're going to let everybody do their own thing.’ This was in some ways a test case.” Trump’s targeted support for Graham — the kind that some Republicans are banking on to shift the dial later this fall — paid off for her in dividends on election night. Horry County, the site of the president’s marquee rally with the candidate late last week, resoundingly broke for Graham. Trump’s backing also helped open the door to endorsements from key South Carolina Republican figures, including fellow GOP Sen. Tim Scott, who helped Graham shore up support in his Charleston-area home base, Gov. Henry McMaster, and two members of the state’s congressional delegation, Reps. Russell Fry and William Timmons. Outside spending also proved crucial to Graham’s success. Her campaign and its allies outspent Norman by more than $5 million in the runoff alone, according to AdImpact . Trump’s allies took a victory lap after Graham’s victory was confirmed Tuesday evening. “The power of the Trump endorsement is alive and well in South Carolina,” said Mike Hahn, a GOP strategist involved in the midterms. “A good opening salvo for the team at MAGA Inc. and the president ahead of the midterms.”
articles.headline: ‘It's put up or shut up time’: Battleground Republicans want the Darline treatment

articles.body: Former state Sen. Mike Mazzei narrowly won Oklahoma’s GOP gubernatorial primary Tuesday, boosted by President Donald Trump’s endorsement, a significant personal loan and a host of outside money. His defeat of Oklahoma Attorney General Gentner Drummond on Tuesday is a victory for Republican leaders in the state and Trump, who had endured a recent string of uncharacteristic primary losses, particularly in gubernatorial primaries. The president’s preferred picks for governor in Wyoming, Iowa, Georgia, Minnesota and South Carolina all lost their races, and a trio of Trump-backed House candidates fell in Michigan and Florida earlier this month. Trump endorsed Mazzei in May, ahead of the state’s open primary, but the race remained competitive. Drummond beat Mazzei by 0.3 percentage points in the first round on June 16, forcing Tuesday’s runoff. And the race was defined by massive levels of self-funding in a historically expensive primary for the state. Mazzei loaned his campaign $11.6 million, while Drummond loaned himself $3 million, according to campaign finance records. But Mazzei was also aided by outside money: The conservative group Club For Growth spent $8 million on TV ads boosting Mazzei and attacking Drummond, per the tracking firm AdImpact. Ahead of the runoff, the state senator earned endorsements from Gov. Kevin Stitt and Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin, who represented Oklahoma in Congress for 13 years. Mazzei served in the state senate for 12 years before being term-limited in 2016. He joined Stitt’s administration for a year in 2019 as budget secretary. He’s the overwhelming favorite in a general election matchup against Democratic state Rep. Cyndi Munson in a state Trump won by 34 points in 2024.
articles.headline: Trump-backed candidate wins primary for Oklahoma governor

articles.body: Sen. Darline Graham defeated Rep. Ralph Norman in South Carolina’s snap Senate GOP primary, a significant win for President Donald Trump after a string of his endorsed candidates stumbled in recent weeks. The president went to great lengths to get her over the finish line: He encouraged her to get into the race with his early endorsement, reiterated that support as she fumbled on the debate stage, and rallied for her in Myrtle Beach — a step that he hasn’t taken for most of his preferred candidates this cycle. The support didn’t stop there. MAGA Inc., Trump’s behemoth super PAC, spent over $827,000 on phone calls and text messages for Graham, money that Republicans in competitive battlegrounds have been anxiously waiting for. Her victory proves that Trump’s backing is still a decisive force in Republican politics when he chooses to give his candidate of choice unwavering and active support. Graham will replace her late brother, Lindsey Graham, on the ballot in November as the Republican nominee. She is all but guaranteed election to a full Senate term in deep red South Carolina. Trump’s loyal backing proved crucial for Graham in the two-week runoff sprint, after a debate stage fumble on foreign policy led Norman and his allies to attack her for her political inexperience. The president’s appearance alongside Graham at a rally in the final days of the race allowed her to close out the primary by reiterating her close ties to Trump. Graham’s win is a remarkable coup for a figure who was unknown to the public just a few weeks ago. She had no prior experience in elected office until she was appointed to the Senate by GOP Gov. Henry McMaster after her brother Lindsey died unexpectedly in July. Since 2019, she has led South Carolina’s Commission for the Blind and had previously worked for the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department. Norman, meanwhile, is a Freedom Caucus stalwart who’s served nine years in Congress and clashed with Trump occasionally over spending — though he’s largely backed the president’s agenda. In the end, his experience didn’t win over voters, and he also saw backlash from the solar industry, which spent $1 million to help defeat him.
articles.headline: Political newcomer Darline Graham wins South Carolina’s GOP Senate runoff

articles.body: Donald Trump is facing one of his biggest tests of the midterms — and it’s of his own making. The president has spent a significant amount of time and money trying to help Sen. Darline Graham defeat Rep. Ralph Norman in Tuesday’s snap GOP Senate primary. He’s done more for Graham than he has for the battleground Republicans whose general election fights will determine control of Congress: Not only did he push her to run for a full term , he also held a rare in-person rally for her and tapped into his MAGA Inc. warchest during the final days of the race. If, after lending all that support, Graham fails, it would be Trump’s most embarrassing loss of the cycle. A win, however, would let him flex his ability to power an unknown political figure to office. “If Darline does come up short, it would be just a massive, massive embarrassment to the White House and to the president. Just an utter rejection,” said Matthew Bartlett, a Republican strategist and former Trump State Department appointee during his first term. Tuesday’s runoff to replace the late Sen. Lindsey Graham on the November ballot won’t meaningfully affect the balance of power in Washington. What it will do is reveal the extent of Trump’s clout, because of just how much personal political capital he has expended in the race to convince voters to elect a virtual stranger. “The fact that he came to the state on short notice to do a rally, and we haven’t seen that in a lot of endorsements, I think that sends a very strong message that he’s all in,” said Andrew Boucher, a GOP strategist and chair of South Carolina’s Charleston County Republican Party, who is neutral in the race. Trump has framed the race as nothing less than a referendum on himself. Rallying with Graham in Myrtle Beach last week, the president told voters to “pretend, please, that I’m on the ballot.” On Monday, a Federal Election Commission report revealed that Trump’s super PAC had spent $827,000 on text messages and phone calls for Graham. It’s one of the largest expenditures this cycle from MAGA Inc., and cash that Republicans in battlegrounds are anxiously awaiting for themselves. One national Republican operative, who was granted anonymity to candidly discuss the president’s influence on the race, noted just how far Trump’s support has gotten Graham: “She wouldn't even be in this place if she didn't have [his support]. The outside help she's had has kind of made this competitive.” Before GOP Gov. Henry McMaster appointed her to serve out the remainder of her late brother’s term in July, Graham was a complete political novice. Graham has worked for the South Carolina Vocational Rehabilitation Department and has led the Commission for the Blind since 2019, but she had never held or even sought public office — a fact that her opponents have attacked her for repeatedly on the campaign trail, especially after she stumbled over a key foreign policy question on the debate stage earlier this month. Her clearest connection to electoral politics lay solely in being the late senator’s younger sister. Trump’s past mistakes in South Carolina loom over the race. The Senate primary has echoes of the state’s governor’s contest earlier this summer, in which Lt. Gov. Pamela Evette, a little-known Trump-backed candidate, fell to the more well-known Attorney General Alan Wilson. As public polling began to show Evette trailing significantly in the first days of that runoff, Trump issued a rare dual endorsement to include Wilson . Evette’s defeat, coupled with a batch of uncharacteristic losses by Trump endorsees in GOP primaries in Georgia, Iowa, Minnesota, Wyoming and Michigan, has put all the more attention on Graham. The power of his endorsement is on the president’s own mind, too. In a Sunday night post on Truth Social , Trump mused that his “Endorsements are stronger than ever,” pointing to splashy charts comparing his wins to his comparatively few defeats. But in the same breath, he acknowledged that his power is not always absolute: “The few that lost were done out of loyalty. It was almost impossible for them to win but, I felt obligated to go with them because they were, in my opinion, good people!” When asked for comment, a White House spokesperson pointed to specific remarks from Trump’s speech at Friday’s rally with Graham, including his acknowledgement that he urged her to jump in the primary. “She’s never done it before, but she knows politics well,” Trump told supporters on Myrtle Beach. “She loves our military. She loves things that have to do with greatness for America.” Graham’s foreign policy debate flub — in which she said “national security is not my thing” in response to a question of U.S. interests in Taiwan — revealed the pitfalls of running for office with no prior experience. Norman has taken advantage of that stumble by hammering her inexperience. The closing stretch of the race has been characterized by Graham trying to tie herself to Trump and burnish her conservative credentials across the state. Norman has tried to shore up support in his Upstate stronghold and expand into the Low Country where former Gov. Mark Sanford — who endorsed his campaign late last week — dominated in the first round. Norman’s also taken to Fox News to bash Graham as an “unknown” and “propped-up candidate.” Graham’s campaign hopes to consolidate support from Rep. Russell Fry’s (R-S.C.) district after he endorsed her campaign a few days into the runoff. Her closing ad of the race claims Norman “turned his back on Trump’s agenda” and is interspersed with footage of her on the rally stage alongside the president. The GOP party establishment in South Carolina has fallen in line behind Graham. Sen. Tim Scott (R-S.C.) publicly backed her bid on the first day of the runoff, Evette got in line shortly thereafter and McMaster followed several days later. Graham’s campaign has itself spent just over $1 million in ads since the outset of the race, but that spending is bolstered by at least three other outside groups — including Security is Strength PAC, Palmetto Action PAC, and American Mission PAC — who also supported her late brother’s primary bid earlier this year. Their spending has topped $6 million, according to AdImpact. Norman has had his own outside help from a notable figure and longtime ally: Former U.N. Ambassador Nikki Haley and her aligned groups have spent more than $700,000 for Norman, including $200,000 on a supportive ad from her issue advocacy group, Stand for America. But that’s still much lower compared with what Graham has received. “Sen. Scott engaging in the race, the congressional delegation, all these portions of it. Congressman Fry engaging in the race is a big deal. You could almost say that's the opposite of what you had in the governor's race,” said a South Carolina-based Republican operative, who was granted anonymity to speak candidly and is staying neutral in the race. Spokespeople for Graham and Norman did not respond to requests for comment.   Graham is still somewhat dogged by her high-profile debate stage mistake, though she’s tried to redirect the attention in interviews. “You know what I’ve done in the last week? I’ve gone around this entire state talking to as many people as I possibly can. And you know how many of them brought up Taiwan and national security? Not one!” she said at a press conference in Columbia on Monday. The late August runoff date could prove unpredictable for both candidates as they seek to drive out their supporters across the state. The twilight of South Carolina’s sticky, slow summer is in full effect: Most kids have returned to school, families across the state are packing their beach gear for one final getaway and the doldrums of summer are still in full force. Several Republicans said that could mean a lower turnout — which could be a boon for a known-quantity candidate with a long history in local office, like Norman. “A lot of the candidates that have defeated Trump-endorsed folks across the map this cycle, they're well-known entities,” said the national GOP operative. “It's hard to overcome some of the basics of politics, where name ID goes a long way. Familiarity with the candidate matters. Having a favorable view and someone who aligns with your values more matters, even if there's a Trump endorsement.” Samuel Benson contributed to this report.
articles.headline: South Carolina could give Trump a revitalizing win — or his most embarrassing loss

articles.body: Michigan Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed put some distance between himself and his ally, progressive Twitch streamer Hasan Piker, after the latter faced intense criticism for suggesting that American Jewish support for Israel could lead someone to “take action” against Jews in the U.S. “My commitment to Jewish safety is the same as my commitment to the safety of my own daughters. Antisemitism is a scourge, and we need to address it in all its forms. And I stand against any rhetoric that puts the community at risk,” El-Sayed said in a statement . “But I want to be crystal clear, nobody speaks for this campaign besides me and my campaign spokespeople. And while politicians and pundits try to make this race about a Twitch streamer, we're going to be talking about gas, groceries, good schools, and healthcare.” The statement marks El-Sayed’s clearest attempt to disentangle his campaign from Piker, whom he embraced during the primary despite the streamer’s contentious rhetoric. And it reflects his efforts to win back Jewish Democrats and moderates in the state after a primary campaign that alienated many of those voters in the key Senate race. During a Thursday livestream, Piker called “the idea that Jews are monolithic” in their support of Israel “a very dangerous mode of propaganda.”“If Jews in America keep putting this — this idea out there that they are singularly invested in Israel, eventually someone’s going to come around and take action, not against the state of Israel, mind you, but against American Jews,” he continued. “We're teaching people the wrong lesson. At the end of the day, American Jews do not prioritize Israel, but they do prioritize antisemitism.” During Piker’s remarks, the stream displayed a social media post showing Michigan Democratic congressional nominee and state Sen. Jeremy Moss, who is Jewish and a supporter of Israel . The post originated from the group Track AIPAC, and featured an image from Moss’ Instagram account of him in Tel Aviv next to the group’s signature red graphic noting contributions from “pro-Israel donors” to Moss’ campaign. Moss’ support for Israel has made him a lightning rod among progressives opposed to pro-Israel Democrats. An audio clip alleged to be a recording of Moss claiming the purpose of his campaign is to maintain U.S. support for Israel went viral online over the weekend. Moss told The Detroit News that it was a fake , and that “I would never say these things.” In a statement Monday evening , Moss said he’s been “in continual dialogue” with El-Sayed, including about “Jewish and Arab safety and security, both here at home in Michigan and in the Middle East.” Moss also denounced Piker’s comments as an attempt to “create further divisions.” “I will not be lectured by a California podcaster about what Oakland County, Michigan's Jewish community should and shouldn't believe," he said. El-Sayed has struggled to unify Michigan Democrats since edging out a victory in a bitter primary that was marked by accusations of antisemitism — partly due to his own views on Israel, and partly due his embrace of Piker, who has risen to prominence through controversial and vocal attacks on Israel. El-Sayed also drew criticisms from the Jewish community for his response after a man attacked a Michigan synagogue in March. El-Sayed condemned the attack but pointed out the Israeli military killed some of the attacker’s family in Lebanon, saying “hurt people hurt people.” . He also received blowback for declining repeatedly to answer whether Israel has a right to exist during a CNN interview in June. His primary campaign made Stevens’ acceptance of contributions from the American Israel Public Affairs Committee a central issue, accusing the group of unfairly influencing the race and steering the party towards stronger U.S. relations with Israel, which he opposes. AIPAC spent $30 million in the race, a record for the group. El-Sayed has repeatedly condemned antisemitism throughout his campaign. His failure to corral support from many Jewish voters in Michigan threatens to undermine Democrats’ chances of winning the Senate. The state’s significant Muslim and Arab-American population and its prominent Jewish population pose unique challenges for Democrats’ messaging around Israel — a problem then-Vice President Kamala Harris struggled to navigate in the 2024 presidential election. Piker’s comments drew a forceful rebuke from Rep. Hillary Scholten (D-Mich.), who endorsed El-Sayed’s opponent Rep. Haley Stevens in the primary and has so far declined to endorse El-Sayed, excoriating Piker’s comments as “dangerous” and “unacceptable.” “Piker is a hack who thrives on hate, shock and awe because he lacks substance,” she said . “We should all be calling out this disgusting rhetoric so it loses it's [sic] grip on our politics once and for all. It has no place in Michigan, and no place in our country.” Piker fired back at Scholten on social media , telling her not to “spend so much time vying for the spotlight by actively defaming a prominent antizionist voice to harm the dem senate majority chances over a 90/10 issue.” Scholten’s statement accused Piker of “targeting” Moss after Piker displayed images of Moss while making the inflammatory comments. Moss, who is running to succeed El-Sayed’s primary opponent Rep. Haley Stevens, backed Stevens in the primary and has yet to endorse El-Sayed in the general election. Republican Mike Rogers jumped on the controversy, describing Piker as El-Sayed’s “running mate.” “Hasan Piker's call for violence against the Jewish Community, specifically against Jeremy Moss, must be condemned by every single Michigan Democrat. But Conman Abdul El-Sayed doesn't have the guts to disavow his running mate,” Rogers said in a statement . “Abdul's attempt at distancing himself from this violent and hateful rhetoric now that he and Hasan won the primary is the epitome of what a conman does — says one thing when it serves him and another when it doesn't.” Since winning the nomination earlier this month, El-Sayed has taken steps to keep Piker at arm’s length. In an August interview, El-Sayed disavowed Piker’s comments that “America deserved 9/11” during a 2019 livestream, a comment Piker has since walked back. Democrats have gone to great lengths to reunify the party after the primary, including with a party unity rally featuring remarks from prominent Michigan Democrats, including unity breakfast Sen. Elissa Slotkin and a rally featuring remarks from former Transportation Secretary Pete Buttigieg. Former President Barack Obama spoke with El-Sayed after his victory and offered a rare readout of the conversation to reporters to signal that El-Sayed has the party’s backing. This article has been updated with Moss' response to Piker's comments.
articles.headline: Abdul El-Sayed distances himself from Hasan Piker’s comments on American Jews

articles.body: President Donald Trump is using a bit of his mostly untapped $400 million MAGA Inc. warchest to boost Sen. Darline Graham in South Carolina — the first significant expenditure his team has made this year for one of his chosen candidates, according to campaign finance reports. The super PAC has funneled more than $827,000 on voter phone calls and text messages for Graham ahead of her tough GOP runoff battle with Rep. Ralph Norman on Tuesday, according to a Federal Election Commission report made public on Monday. It’s yet another sign that Trump is focusing his efforts on propelling Graham — a political newcomer — to victory, after holding a rare in-person political rally with her on Friday. And it’s a notable spend given MAGA Inc.’s ongoing absence from other battleground races this cycle, even as Republicans have been pushing the president and his team to spend heavily this fall to help counter Democrats’ massive fundraising advantage. As of last week, the super PAC had reported over $403 million in fundraising. The money for Graham is just the second time MAGA Inc. has spent on a race this year. The group in March shelled out nearly $18,000 for now-Rep. Clay Fuller (R-Ga.), who was running in the special election to replace former Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene. And in late 2025, MAGA Inc. threw roughly $1.7 million into phone calls for Tennessee Republican Matt Van Epps, who won the special election to replace retired Rep. Mark Green (R-Tenn.). Spokespeople for MAGA Inc. and the White House did immediately respond to requests for comment. Should Graham become the Republican nominee in South Carolina on Tuesday, it will be in large part thanks to Trump, who expended serious political and financial capital to help her win. Her victory would also help reaffirm Trump’s influence in Republican primaries after a string of losses for his preferred candidates in states like Michigan, Minnesota, and Iowa. Jessica Piper contributed to this report.

articles.body: (ACN/Redacció) Les cambreres de pis dels hotels, popularment conegudes com a ‘kellys’, s’han manifestat aquest dimarts a la tarda, a la plaça de Sant Jaume, per exigir millores laborals. “Som treballadores, no esclaves” , “Sense ‘kellys’ no hi ha turisme” o “no a l’externalització” han estat els missatges que han mostrat en diverses pancartes, per denunciar que les seves condicions “van a pitjor” mentre el sector turístic bat rècords . Per aquest motiu han demanat “empatia” a la patronal. “Com pot ser que amb els beneficis que obté la gran indústria hotelera tothom hi guanyi menys nosaltres?”, s’ha preguntat la portaveu de Kellys Unió Catalunya, Juani Pérez. Després de més d’una dècada protestant cada 25 d’agost, han celebrat haver guanyat visibilitat, però ara reclamen fets. També han explicat que les seves condicions laborals són “molt precàries ” i que tenen una càrrega de treball que qualifiquen de desproporcionada , i que s’agreuja a l’estiu. Fins i tot, han mostrat imatges de l’estat amb què, sovint, es troben les habitacions. “Ens toca sortir a recordar, un any més, que continuem aquí i que continuem patint”, ha sentenciat Pérez. articles.body: Un incendi s’ha declarat al Parc de Collserola , al districte de Nou Barris per sobre de la carretera Alta de Roquetes . Fonts municipals han detallat que el foc està en fase d’estabilització . Per la proximitat de les flames, l’Ajuntament de Barcelona ha confirmat que s’ha desallotjat de forma preventiva els veïns dels carrers de Lliçà i Castellví , a Torre Baró. Es tracta d’una vintena d’habitatges, els que estan més a prop de la frontera amb la zona forestal, on el foc està actiu. En total, s’han evacuat 35 persones. Prèviament també s’ha declarat el confinament preventiu dels veïns de la zona de Torre Baró i Ciutat Meridiana. Segons han detallat fonts municipals, els efectius ja saben per on crema el foc i per on pot avançar, i consideren que no perillen altres edificis ni es preveuen més desallotjaments. Al llarg d’aquest dimarts a la nit refrescaran les zones de l’incendi i vigilaran els flancs del foc.  També et pot interessar Bombers de Barcelona: “Estem treballant perquè el foc no arribi a les cases” Mar Arans 1 minut de lectura 35 hectàrees cremades En les tasques d’extinció hi han participat una setantena d’unitats dels bombers . En concret, són 27 dotacions dels Bombers de Barcelona i 46 del cos dels Bombers de la Generalitat , entre les quals dotze mitjans aeris . Durant la nit els mitjans aeris han deixat de treballar, però reprendran les tasques dimecres al matí. L’incendi continua actiu però està en fase d’estabilització i els bombers esperen que en les properes hores les condicions ambientals millorin i puguin controlar-ne els flancs. ”Estem treballant perquè el foc no arribi a les cases , però en tot cas, si passés, som allà”, ha explicat Sergi Bové, el cap d’intervenció dels Bombers de Barcelona. El foc s’ha declarat en una zona de matolls poc després de les tres de la tarda i ha afectat una línia d’alta tensió del parc. Segons el darrer balanç ja han cremat 35 hectàrees . En una compareixença als mitjans, Collboni ha assegurat que confia que els efectius desplaçats aconsegueixin controlar l’incendi. Confinament preventiu a Torre Baró i Ciutat Meridiana Protecció Civil ha declarat el confinament preventiu dels veïns de Torre Baró i Ciutat Meridiana. El confinament no és per una possible arribada del foc a la zona sinó pel fum que sí que pot afectar els residents. Veïns de la zona han rebut dos missatges al telèfon mòbil d’ ES-Alert en què els han avisat del confinament. Alguns, però, s’han trobat amb la notícia in situ , quan volien accedir a la zona i els Mossos d’Esquadra no els han permès arran d’aquest confinament. I demanen a la resta de la ciutadania que no s’acosti a la zona. Davant de qualsevol emergència, recomanen trucar al 112 , un telèfon que ja ha atès 380 trucades . El Centre Cívic de Torre Baró acull els veïns desallotjats Per ara s’han desallotjat els veïns d’una vintena d’habitatges. L’Ajuntament ha habilitat el Centre Cívic de Torre Baró per tal d’acollir-hi els afectats i, d’altres veïns que viuen més avall també s’han ofert a acollir-los. articles.body: Catalunya ha viscut aquest dilluns un gran temporal que ha escombrat bona part del territori amb nombrosos danys materials que han afectat principalment al Camp de Tarragona . Un episodi que ha provocat inundacions , pedrades i fortes ventades . Tot plegat, mentre un tornado també ha sacsejat el sud de França i ha provocat importants afectacions al seu pas. Barcelona s’ha salvat i no li ha tocat rebre. Tot i això, els experts alerten que aquests fenòmens seran cada vegada més freqüents i intensos a tot el món, alhora que difícils de preveure . També et pot interessar El Meteocat avisa: les altes temperatures podrien convertir-se en la normalitat a finals de segle Andrea Muñoz 3 minuts de lectura Segons Carme Vidal, catedràtica de física de la Universitat de Barcelona , aquests fenòmens són molt difícils de predir, principalment, perquè “són molt localitzats i els mapes no els detecten bé, alhora que són molt curts “. En aquest sentit, alerta que encara és més complicat fer una predicció de la intensitat d’aquests episodis. És a dir, “quina serà la grandària de la pedra, quants litres de pluja cauran o, fins i tot, si es formaran grans tornados”. Per això, Vidal argumenta que el Servei Meteorològic de Catalunya pot elevar la perillositat dels avisos meteorològics en funció de com avancen els episodis . De fet, “és el que sol passar i, per tant, Protecció Civil no pot estar constantment enviant alertes a la població “, afegeix. En qualsevol cas, insisteix que s’ha millorat molt la predicció en els darrers anys i que tant Protecció Civil com el Meteocat informen constantment dels perills. També et pot interessar Avisos meteorològics: qui els fa i com es fan? Lluís Cruz Berasategui 3 minuts de lectura Què fa que els episodis siguin cada vegada més violents? Vidal també apunta que els fenòmens meteorològics adversos són i seran cada vegada més intensos . I, això perquè? Segons l’experta, per culpa de el canvi climàtic , que fa augmentar les temperatures . En concret, quan puja la temperatura, també puja la humitat i això provoca que l’aigua es condensi i es torni líquida o, fins i tot, en pedra. Quan això passa s’allibera calor i aquesta és l’energia que ajuda que els temporals siguin més virulents. Això vol dir, per exemple, que “el que podria ser una tempesta d’estiu, es converteixi en un episodi sever “, afegeix. Davant d’aquest escenari, Vidal fa una crida a combatre el canvi climàtic i lluitar perquè “les temperatures no continuïn pujant”. Per això, demana més prevenció i conscienciació ciutadana per reduir les crisis meteorològiques. articles.body: Un estudi coordinat per l’ Institut de Recerca Sant Pau i el Centre d’Integració de Dades i Coneixements per a la Salut del Brasil evidencia que l’exposició a la sequera durant l’embaràs s’associa a un augment del risc de part prematur . En els casos de sequeres prolongades, també s’ha detectat una major probabilitat de creixement fetal insuficient . 30 milions de naixements analitzats La recerca ha analitzat prop de 30 milions de naixements registrats al Brasil entre el 2001 i el 2020 . Tot i que la investigació s’ha dut a terme al país sud-americà, els autors assenyalen que els resultats poden ser rellevants per a altres regions cada cop més exposades a períodes de sequera i temperatures extremes. És el cas de la conca mediterrània, on aquests fenòmens poden ser cada vegada més freqüents com a conseqüència del canvi climàtic. També et pot interessar Prematurs extrems reben sang de cordó umbilical en un assaig de l’Hospital Clínic Redaccio Societat 3 minuts de lectura Risc de creixement fetal insuficient L’anàlisi també mostra que les sequeres prolongades, d’entre sis i nou mesos, es relacionen amb un increment d’entre l’1 % i el 2 % en la probabilitat que el nadó sigui petit per a la seva edat gestacional. Aquest efecte és especialment evident quan l’exposició a la sequera es produeix durant les fases inicial i intermèdia de l’embaràs, períodes clau per al desenvolupament fetal. L’estudi apunta, a més, que quan la sequera coincideix amb episodis de calor extrema , el risc de part prematur augmenta encara més . La vulnerabilitat socioeconòmica, un factor clau Els resultats també evidencien que les condicions socioeconòmiques poden incrementar la vulnerabilitat davant dels fenòmens climàtics extrems. La manca de recursos pot dificultar l’accés a aigua potable, mantenir una alimentació adequada o garantir un seguiment prenatal regular. articles.body: Els missatges fraudulents cada cop són més freqüents en el nostre dia a dia: a través de correus electrònics, SMS o fins i tot paquets que t’envien a casa , els ciberdelinqüents busquen la manera d’accedir a les nostres dades. L’ Agència de Ciberseguretat de Catalunya alerta que any rere any hi ha un augment d’estafes i que, enguany, s’ha creat una nova modalitat: les estafes híbrides. “Són les que combinen el món digital amb el món físic”, explica Txell Collado, cap de la Unitat de Comunicació de l’Agència de Ciberseguretat de Catalunya. Un exemple és l’entrega de paquets amb un QR a dins que, en escanejar-lo, et dirigeix a una web fraudulenta. També et pot interessar Repunten els robatoris de comptes de WhatsApp: aquests són els consells dels Mossos per evitar-los Eva Vial 3 minuts de lectura “Amb el format híbrid , els estafadors tenen més maneres de pressionar les persones. Si reps un missatge i just després reps una trucada que es fan passar pel banc, ja tens dues verificacions. Aquesta sensació d’urgència no et deixa pensar amb tranquil·litat i aquesta mateixa pressió et porta a l’estafa”, afegeix. La intel·ligència artificial juga a favor dels delinqüents Un dels factors que més amoïna l’Agència és que cada cop més, afirmen, costa identificar un missatge fraudulent. “Es difícil adonar-nos de l’estafa perquè amb la intel·ligència artificial ara costa molt”. Anteriorment, les faltes d’ortografia o missatges incoherents podien delatar els estafadors. Ara, amb l’ús de la IA, els delinqüents han pogut perfeccionar les seves tècniques dificultant, així, la feina de l’Agència. També et pot interessar Expert en ciberseguretat: “El robatori de dades permet estafes més creïbles” Andrea Cuerva Bonich 2 minuts de lectura Què podem fer si sospitem que hem rebut una estafa? Quan rebem un missatge que sospitem que pot ser una estafa, el que cal fer és no ser impulsiu: “ Aturem-nos pensem 10 segons, 20 segons, 30 segons abans de fer res”, recomana Collado. I és que el més important és no caure en la sensació d’urgència que ens traslladen els estafadors. “Cal desconfiar de tot i, si es necessari, ens demanen fer una acció urgent, validar-ho per un altre canal abans de clicar res”, afegeix. Una trucada al banc per assegurar-nos que no hi ha cap problema és suficient per no caure en el parany dels estafadors. articles.body: El Barça femení disputarà el Clàssic contra el Real Madrid al Camp Nou el pròxim 4 d’octubre , segons ha confirmat oficialment la Lliga F . El duel correspondrà a la sisena jornada del campionat i, de moment, encara no té un horari definit. La decisió confirma els plans que ja havia avançat Xavi Puig , directiu responsable del futbol femení blaugrana, que havia expressat la voluntat del club de portar els partits més destacats de l’equip al Camp Nou . El duel del 4 d’octubre serà, per tant, el tercer enfrontament entre els dos equips en aquest escenari i reforçarà l’aposta del Barça perquè el seu equip femení jugui més partits al Camp Nou .

articles.body: L’Ajuntament de Barcelona ja encara la transformació de l’antic recinte fabril de La Escocesa amb l’objectiu que estigui en ple funcionament el 2029 . L’espai, ubicat al 22@nord, al Poblenou, serà un “ecosistema creatiu i un pol econòmic per a la ciutat”, tal com ha destacat l’alcalde Jaume Collboni en una roda de premsa al Saló de Cent de l’Ajuntament aquest dimarts. El projecte municipal per a l’espai de La Escocesa renovarà 11.528 metres quadrats , amb una inversió mínima de 51,8 milions d’euros. D’aquesta xifra, 27,2 milions d’euros seran aportats per l’Ajuntament de Barcelona, que compta amb la col·laboració d’administracions públiques, el sector cultural, el tercer sector i el món empresarial per a la transformació de l’antic recinte. Construcció d’habitatge inclusiu L’objectiu per a aquest espai és crear “un sistema de serveis interconnectats” que comptaran amb tres eixos principals: l’economia, les cures i la cultura. Aquests serveis es dividiran entre les set naus que estan en procés de renovació. En concret, algunes de les naus es transformarà en un edifici d’habitatges assistits per a persones amb discapacitat . A més, també hi haurà un espai que acollirà un centre d’art inclusiu, amb activitats que reforçaran la inserció laboral d’aquests col·lectius. L’objectiu d’aquesta àrea, destaca el consistori, és “ fomentar l’acció comunitària i l’enxarxament veïnal” entre col·lectius vulnerables. També et pot interessar L’Ajuntament vol transformar La Escocesa: hi haurà habitatges i projectes d’economia social Marina Segura i Vidal 2 minuts de lectura Espai de creació i innovació econòmica A més d’aquest espai de creació amb una mirada inclusiva, dues de les naus de La Escocesa ja funcionen com a fàbrica de creació , amb més de 30 artistes residents en un espai gestionat col·lectivament. L’any 2024 es van organitzar més de 40 activitats públiques, una xifra que s’espera que s’amplïi a mesura que es rehabilita per complert la nau destinada a la creació. A banda, l’objectiu és crear el Barcelona Foodlab , un centre d’incubació i recerca en l’àmbit de la tecnologia alimentària. El centre, que combinarà aules formatives i espais de cotreball, ha estat impulsat per l’Ajuntament de Barcelona, a través de Barcelona Activa, conjuntament amb Mercabarna i la Generalitat de Catalunya. Aquesta col·laboració vol consolidar els nous projectes emprenedors amb la indústria agroalimentària, acompanyant també en la creació d’empreses en el sector. Finalment, una de les naus serà un pol d’economia social i solidària (ESS) gestionat col·lectivament per entitats que se centrin en visibilitzar l’ESS com una alternativa econòmica, així com reforçar la cooperació entre entitats i fomentar les energies renovables i l’eficiència energètica.

articles.body: El centre de Barcelona comptarà, a partir del proper novembre, amb un nou teatre centrat, especialment, en l’humor, i on també hi haurà lloc per a la dansa, els espectacles familiars i el flamenc. El Teatre Balmes obrirà portes al carrer de Balmes, a l’illa de cases entre Rosselló i Còrsega . La programació arrencarà amb monòlegs d’humor com Escocía , de Txabi Franquesa o Yo sobreviví a EGB , de Jordi Merca, a més d’espectacles com Se ha escrito un crimen ,  El nuevo musical de los 80-90 o Vaga y maleanta , de Kiki Morgan. A més, els gestors del nou espai han tancat acords amb el col·lectiu Churros con Chocolate i amb la companyia de teatre juvenil El Aedo. La sala també oferirà produccions familiars i funcions escolars i preveu arribar a fer fins a tres espectacles al dia. El Teatre Balmes ofereix la possibilitat d’inscriure’s al Club Balmes , que ofereix descomptes, accessos exclusius i sorteigs, entre d’altres prestacions. Inaugurat com a cinema a principis del segle passat, ha sigut també el teatre Parthenon, abans de convertir-se, primer en el Palacio del Flamenco i, després, en el Tablao de la Pacheca. En la seva nova etapa, la reforma de les instal·lacions ha suposat unes butaques mòbils que permeten habilitar un espai central per a dansa i cafè teatre . articles.body: Nou pas en les obres de transformació del recinte firal de Montjuïc. Aquest dilluns, 24 d’agost, ha arrencat l’ enderrocament de la cúpula del pavelló 4 del recinte, conegut com el pavelló Rius i Taulet, segons ha confirmat el Departament d’Economia. Les imatges a què ha tingut accés betevé han estat enregistrades des de l’aire amb un dron, i capten el moment en què la grua que treballa sobre la coberta, amb un braç de 60 metres i de fet una de les més grans d’Europa, fa una mossegada que acaba ensorrant tota l’estructura. L’enderroc d’aquest espai, però, no és nou. Va arrencar fa un mes, el 28 de juliol, amb les primeres demolicions. El desmuntatge de la cúpula és el pas més visible fins ara dels treballs en aquest pavelló, que va guanyar notorietat durant la pandèmia de covid com a gran centre de vacunació de la ciutat . També et pot interessar Nou pas en la remodelació del recinte firal de Montjuïc: comencen a enderrocar pavellons Núria Granados 3 minuts de lectura El pavelló Rius i Taulet se situa al costat del Palau de Congressos de la Fira, que també té els dies comptats. Tots dos espais aniran a terra per fer lloc al nou palau multifuncional que ha de vertebrar el recinte renovat. El nou equipament tindrà dues plantes i 20.500 m² de superfície amb una  gran passarel·la enjardinada  que unirà els dos pavellons. El projecte, a més, també inclou la renovació i ampliació del Palau 1. Objectiu 2029 Aquesta actuació forma part de la gran transformació de la Fira de Montjuïc , que s’allargarà fins al 2029, amb l’objectiu de tenir el recinte renovat per al centenari de l’Exposició Internacional . El calendari d’obres afecta diversos pavellons i inclou, entre d’altres, la construcció d’un nou amfiteatre de congressos al Palau Alfons XIII i la reforma del Palau Victòria Eugènia.
